# respR -- an R package for the analysis of respirometry data {#package}
\chaptermark{respR -- an R package for respirometry}

<!-- {\small -->
<!-- This chapter is formatted for Methods in Ecology and Evolution. It is under review as "Harianto J, Carey N and Byrne M (2018). respR -- an R package for the analysis of respirometry data." The R package, \texttt{respR}, has been published on GitHub as an open-source project. -->
<!-- } -->



## Abstract {-}

\begin{enumerate}
	\item Respirometry is a ubiquitous practice in experimental biology, but there is a lack of standard practices when analysing the resulting data, limiting transparency and reproducibility. As respirometry datasets become increasingly large and analytical approaches more complex, manipulating the data remains a challenge and often intractable with existing tools.
	\item Here we describe the \texttt{respR} R package, a collection of functions that implement a workflow-based approach to automate the analysis and visualisation of respirometry data. The package can be used for closed, intermittent flow, flow-through and open-tank respirometry and uses well-defined sets of rules to reliably and rapidly generate reproducible results.
	\item We demonstrate how \texttt{respR} uses novel computing methods such as rolling regressions and kernel density estimates to reliably detect maximum, minimum and most linear sections of the data, and critical oxygen tension, P\textsubscript{crit}.
	\item Although designed specifically with aquatic respirometry in mind, the object-oriented approach of the package and the unit-less nature of its analytical functions mean that parts of the package can easily be used to estimate linear relationships from a range of applications in many research disciplines.
\end{enumerate}
